nodes.Name: pageCache
nodes.DocComment:
pageCache represents a per-p cache of pages the allocator can
allocate from without a lock. More specifically, it represents
a pageCachePages*pageSize chunk of memory with 0 or more free
pages in it.

Fields.Name: cache
Fields.DocComment: 64-bit bitmap representing free pages (1 means free)

Fields.Name: scav
Fields.DocComment: 64-bit bitmap representing scavenged pages (1 means scavenged)

nodes.Name: empty
nodes.DocComment: empty reports whether the page cache has no free pages.

nodes.Name: alloc
nodes.DocComment:
alloc allocates npages from the page cache and is the main entry
point for allocation.

Returns a base address and the amount of scavenged memory in the
allocated region in bytes.

Returns a base address of zero on failure, in which case the
amount of scavenged memory should be ignored.

nodes.Name: allocN
nodes.DocComment:
allocN is a helper which attempts to allocate npages worth of pages
from the cache. It represents the general case for allocating from
the page cache.

Returns a base address and the amount of scavenged memory in the
allocated region in bytes.

nodes.Name: flush
nodes.DocComment:
flush empties out unallocated free pages in the given cache
into s. Then, it clears the cache, such that empty returns
true.

p.mheapLock must be held.

Must run on the system stack because p.mheapLock must be held.

go:systemstack

nodes.Name: allocToCache
nodes.DocComment:
allocToCache acquires a pageCachePages-aligned chunk of free pages which
may not be contiguous, and returns a pageCache structure which owns the
chunk.

p.mheapLock must be held.

Must run on the system stack because p.mheapLock must be held.

go:systemstack
